<subagent sessionID="ses_e4869d4ffffefZKpbmUNHXIH0d" state="completed">
## DNA-to-morphology integration points

- **Genetic schema and inheritance — [`src/genetics.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/genetics.js), lines 1–27, 70–88, 91–120, 313–344.** `GENE_KEYS` and `GENE_META` define the current normalized traits; `crossover()` and `mutate()` determine how genomes are inherited and changed. If morphology needs new alleles, this schema and the linkage groups need to include them. `TRAIT_ROWS` also controls which genes can be selected for directed mutation.

- **DNA and systemic expression — [`src/dna.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/dna.js), lines 8–29.** `encodeGenome()` converts the existing alleles to a display sequence, while `expressSystems()` maps them to muscle, bones, fat, nerves, ears, and other tissue values. This is a natural integration point for shared gene-to-phenotype calculations, but the encoded sequence is currently a visualization encoding—not a separate source of morphology data.

- **Organism morphology and geometry — [`src/creature.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creature.js), lines 150–249 and 283–405.** `Creature.build()` computes systemic expression, overall scale, and organism dimensions, then creates the body. `buildHead()`, `buildTail()`, and `buildLegs()` consume those dimensions and genes to make geometry. The model already responds to body size, neck, legs, tail, armor, crest, and some expressed tissue systems, so these are the most direct places to extend DNA-driven morphology.

- **Cell-stage morphology — [`src/creature.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creature.js), lines 228–230 and 642–721.** `build()` diverts cellular-stage creatures to `buildCell()`, which builds a spherical cell with a fixed set of organelles. Body size affects overall scale, but cellular form and organelle counts are mostly fixed. If the feature should affect both stages, this builder needs its own genotype-to-cell-phenotype mapping.

- **Rebuilding an individual specimen — [`src/creature.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creature.js), lines 878–929; [`src/main.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js), lines 295–307 and 708–727.** `CreatureSystem.replace()` reconstructs the creature at its current stage. Both directed mutations and DNA-bank restoration update the organism’s genome and evaluation, then call this replacement path. Any new expressed traits must be recomputed by the constructor/build path so these interactions display them immediately.

- **Population creation and lifecycle changes — [`src/main.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js), lines 175–195 and 619–640; [`src/creature.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/creature.js), lines 878–898.** `makeOrganism()` creates the simulation object from a genome; `breedPopulation()` in `genetics.js` produces offspring genomes; `spawnPopulation()` rebuilds the visible population at the supplied stage. `advanceGeneration()` changes to `"organism"` at generation 4 and respawns the population, while `resetStudy()` returns it to `"cellular"` ([`src/main.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js), lines 764–779). The lifecycle change is therefore a stage-wide rebuild, not gradual maturation.

- **Genome archive and presentation — [`src/main.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js), lines 210–216, 275–307, and 389–390; [`src/genetics.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/genetics.js), lines 255–289.** Archive validation and saving iterate over `GENE_KEYS`, and the analyzer consumes `analyzeGenome()`. If the genome schema changes, these paths need to remain compatible. Names and dossier labels are also derived from genome traits, but they currently describe traits rather than define species identities.

## Main risks to account for

- **Stage coverage:** an allele added only to organism geometry will have no visible effect during the initial cellular generations. The current stage switch happens at generation 4 and replaces the whole model.
- **Trait coupling and bounds:** dimensions are affected by both direct alleles and systemic expression, and the whole model also receives an overall scale. Large changes can compound. Selection radius is separately derived from `bodySize` (`creature.js`, line 146), so it can stop matching a remodeled body.
- **Rig and movement assumptions:** the organism builder hardcodes four legs and fixed animation/ground behavior. Changing limb lengths or body proportions may require matching updates to joints, feet, animation, and terrain placement—not just mesh dimensions.
- **Schema consistency:** new alleles need coordinated updates to gene metadata, inheritance/linkage, mutation choices, analysis, and archive validation. Archived entries are validated against the current gene list, so schema changes can affect whether older archives restore.
- **Threshold-only expression:** some existing traits add features only above thresholds—for example armor and crest. Intermediate allele changes may not produce gradual visible changes, which can make genotype-to-morphology behavior appear discontinuous.
- **Species identity versus appearance:** `nameCreature()` assigns a name from a small set of threshold checks; there is no separate species classification or persistent species record. If “species creation” means lineage grouping rather than visual variation, that would need a distinct design beyond the existing population-breeding and naming paths.
